newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp new issue calendar continues to build.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp new issue calendar continues to build.

text.p: The calendar for corporate bond issuance continues to build as an improved interest rate environment draws issuers into the primary arena, dealers said.
"There's a very positive upbeat tone to the market," said one high-grade syndicaate source. "The market is down a touch but we've rallied ... we've had a good run for our money so far," he said.
Currently, the U.S. Treasuy 30-year bond is trading off 12/32 at 98-23/32 to yield 6.72 percent, versus 6.69 percent at Monday's close.
Players attributed the drop in U.S. Treasuries to some earlier profit-taking following this morning's release of two U.S. economic indicators, which came in as expected.
On Tuesday, the Labor Department reported a 0.1 percent increase in the U.S. consumer price index for May; excluding food and energy, CPI rose 0.2 percent.
Later, the Commerce Department reported a drop of 4.8 percent in U.S. May housing starts.
The data added to market sentiment that inflation remains under control and that therefore, Federal Reserve policymakers will keep interest rates steady at their next meeting on July 1.
Still, despite the drop in U.S. Treasuries, players said the tone remains upbeat.
"The way we see it is the (Treasury) market adjusts itself a bit, then it rallies, then adjusts itself again, but if you look at it overall, we're up," a syndicate official said.
Although a quiet day is expected in the investment-grade arena, new names continue to pop up adding to the already heavy supply of about $4.0 billion in new debt, players said.
Among new names circulating the primary arena is Toro Co, which is expected to issue $75 million in 10-year debt and $100 million in 30-year debt via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Also, Pohang Iron & Steel is expected to bring $300 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities Inc, players said.
RJR Nabisco is slated to bring $350 million in a two-part debt offering via joint managers Morgan Stanley & Co Inc and Merrill Lynch & Co, syndicate sources said.
The RJR deal is expected to include a $150 million seven-year issue as well as a $200 million 10-year issue.
Consolidated Edison is expected to sell $150 million in A1/A-plus floating rate notes due 2002 via competitive bid on Tuesday, as well, sources said.
In addition, Old Republic International is expected to sell $115 million in Aa2/AA-minus rated 10-year debt via Lehman Brothers, players said.

Among global issuers, Lehman Brothers launched a $500 million A1/A-plus rated seven-year debt offering for American Express, sources said. The deal is expected to price at a spread of 39 to 41 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Another $1.0 billion in AAA rated 10-year gobal debt is expected to come from Bayerische Landesbank via JP Morgan Securities and Merrill Lynch one day this week, they said.
A debt offering for the Republic of South Africa is also slated to be launched this week, players said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, about $1.7 billion in new debt is expected this week, sources said.

The bulk of the issuance is expected to take place in the private placement market, which now comprises slightly above 50 percent of high-yield market issuance, according to research firm Securities Data Co.
So far in the private placement market, Young Broadcasting sold $200 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes at 250 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch.

Also, Outdoor Systems Inc issued $500 million in 10-year 144A notes at 261 basis points over Treasuries via CIBC Wood Gundy, sources said. The deal was upped in size from an initially planned sale of $300 million.
Another $100 million in 10-year 144A notes is expected to be brought to market by Roller Bearing Co of America Inc.
Also, Echostar DBS Corp will sell $325 million in five-year senior secured notes via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities.
In addition, Drypers Corp will sell $115 million in 10-year 144A debt via Prudential Securities. Price talk on the deal is seen between 10.25 and 10.50 percent, they added.

Another $150 million in 144A 10-year senior subordinated notes will be brought by Coach USA Inc and will also be underwritten by DLJ. Price talk on the issue is seen between 9.25 and 9.50 percent, players said.

Among other 144A deals are: Verio Inc's $250 million deal, Chase Telecommunications $125 million offfering, North Atlantic Trading Co's $115 million offering, Equimar Shipholdings Ltd's $100 million issue, Leiner Health Products $85 million issue, and Oxford Automotive Inc's $125 million offering, dealers said.
